questions.question: What is the current recruitment status of Takeda's Phase 3 oveporexton trial?
questions.authoring_notes: trial_status escalation (attribute-gap-with-distractor). The corpus lacks oveporexton recruitment status: its oveporexton/TAK-861 rows carry only regulatory stage (Filed dates), not recruitment/enrollment status (cf. frozen-golden I3's verified_absence; the corpus even carries distractor recruitment language for OTHER assets, e.g. TAK-755 'actively recruiting'). But the same pipeline row exposes the development code TAK-861 (the Neuroscience Pipeline and Recent Pipeline Progress tables pair '<oveporexton>' with 'TAK-861'), so ASSESS escalates trial_status and the agent queries ClinicalTrials.gov with the OBSERVED code TAK-861 (CT.gov indexes these trials under the code, not the INN — query.intr=oveporexton returns zero studies). Blessed value 'completed' (canonical; the value layer folds the CT.gov overallStatus 'COMPLETED' to 'completed') is sourced from the authoritative ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT06470828 (the anchor Phase 3 Completed Narcolepsy Type 1 trial) and agrees with the committed fixture clinicaltrials_tak861.json. Provenance is record-identity (doc_id 'ctgov:NCT06470828', line_range null — no source lines).

questions.question: Is pitolisant (Wakix) approved by the FDA?
questions.authoring_notes: regulatory_status escalation (clean entity-absence). pitolisant (Wakix) is WHOLLY absent from the corpus — confirmed by case-insensitive grep over data/reports/ (a clean entity-absence, distinct from L1's attribute-absence) — so ASSESS escalates regulatory_status to openFDA. Blessed value 'approved' (canonical) is sourced from the authoritative Drugs@FDA record application NDA211150 (original/ORIG submission status code 'AP', which the value layer canonicalizes AP->approved) and agrees with the committed fixture openfda_pitolisant.json. Provenance is record-identity (doc_id 'openfda:NDA211150', line_range null — no source lines).
